primitives.name: Markov Decision Process
primitives.verbatim_quote: This year's theme, predicting where players will move from point A to point B once the ball is in the air.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: s - state (player position and velocity), a - action (movement direction), s' - next state, P - transition probability distribution
primitives.assumptions: The NFL player movement follows a Markov property where future states depend only on the current state and action.

The core challenge is translating high-dimensional spatiotemporal tracking data into actionable predictive models. We leverage the NFL Big Data Bowl's open-source framework to construct a unified state-transition kernel. This kernel integrates Markov Decision Processes for discrete action spaces with Bayesian Graphical Models to infer latent player skills. Conformal Prediction provides robust uncertainty quantification, while Multi-Armed Bandits enable online adaptation. The resulting sovereign primitive operates as a differentiable manifold where each point represents a joint distribution over player positions, actions, and rewards. Empirical validation uses holdout testing on unseen game footage.
